SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient reports onset of low back pain on 06/04/2026. He describes the pain as diffuse lumbar aching worsened by flexion and prolonged standing. He denies radicular symptoms.
Exam: Inspection shows normal lumbar contour; palpation reveals mild paraspinal tenderness; range of motion limited due to discomfort. Neuro exam: normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation.
Assessment: Acute mechanical low back pain, likely degenerative.
Plan: Start NSAIDs today (06/05/2026) for pain control. Referral to physical therapy to begin 06/11/2026. Advise activity modification and follow-up in 2 weeks. No red flags identified.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: He was prescribed NSAIDs starting 06/05/2026 and continued through 07/16/2026 with partial relief. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/11/2026, consisting of 10 sessions completed by 07/16/2026, without symptomatic improvement.
Exam: Similar to prior; mild paraspinal tenderness; neuro exam unchanged: normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, sensation.
Assessment: Persistent mechanical low back pain despite conservative measures. He denies any red flag symptoms such as fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bowel/bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Plan: Continue NSAIDs as needed; consider advanced imaging.

HPI: He completed a course of NSAIDs from 06/05/2026 to 07/16/2026 with partial response, and physical therapy from 06/11/2026 to 07/16/2026 comprising 10 sessions with no improvement.
Exam: Inspection normal; palpation shows mild lumbar tenderness; neuro exam: normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation.
Assessment: Chronic low back pain, unresponsive to NSAIDs and physical therapy.
Plan: Order lumbar MRI to evaluate for structural pathology; pending results, a spine surgery referral will be considered.
